donors.does: compiles desired Boolean target states backward through known causal gate semantics to synthesize minimum input interventions, with exact search fallback on shared upstream structures
donors.exploits: known causal ancestry and operator semantics make much of uninformed intervention enumeration unnecessary
preconditions: the causal graph and equations are supplied
the direct path is tree-like or the exact fallback is used
effects: minimum intervention cardinality is preserved on the preregistered benchmark
median full-model evaluations fall relative to exhaustive search
assumptions: declared Boolean SCM semantics match the tested system
declared controllable inputs are the complete action set

donors.does: compares a proposed primitive's behavior against an existing finite ontology before admitting a novelty challenge
donors.exploits: different names or formulas can denote behaviorally equivalent mechanisms and would otherwise create false novelty
preconditions: candidate behaviors are executable on the same fixtures
effects: exact behavioral equivalents are identified before experiment admission
nearest existing behavior and mismatch rate remain visible
assumptions: finite fixture behavior is useful evidence for local equivalence screening
finite non-equivalence is not universal novelty

donors.does: selects a candidate primitive from a declared meta-family, rejects exact old-ontology equivalents on a finite fixture, and freezes the selected primitive before transfer evaluation
donors.exploits: a representation absent from the old ontology can become a reusable feature if admitted through held-out evidence and semantic novelty gates
preconditions: the meta-family is frozen before held-out results
the target passes semantic novelty preflight against the old ontology
effects: a finite-fixture behaviorally distinct primitive can be admitted
the frozen primitive can be reused across separately held-out tasks
assumptions: the declared meta-family contains useful candidate primitives
synthetic transfer predicts only the narrow tested software mechanism

donors.does: searches a frozen divisor-sweep program grammar and transfers one learned structural program exactly to parity of distinct-prime count on a public external sequence target
donors.exploits: arithmetic properties can sometimes be represented as compact state updates over factorization events rather than memorized labels
preconditions: the structural grammar is frozen before result
public target definitions are fixed independently of search
effects: distinct-prime parity reaches exact held-out transfer
squarefree and Mobius-positive failures expose missing multiplicity memory
assumptions: the public sequence implementation matches the cited definition
the frozen grammar meaningfully represents the tested structural family

donors.does: selects a bounded minimum-reality probe, compiles a preregistration, routes it through canonical experiment feasibility policy, and preserves authority separation
donors.exploits: many research failures come from confusing a plan with an experiment or feasibility with permission
preconditions: a falsifiable claim and competing predicted outcomes exist
candidate probes declare cost time reversibility measurement and decision rule
effects: zero-effect experiments can become runnable without external authority
effectful probes remain blocked when required authority is absent
assumptions: declared probe costs and effects are truthful
observed evidence is reconciled separately from preregistration

donors.does: recognizes exact finite Boolean boundary-equivalent causal subgraphs across different syntax and reuses one verified semantic operator during backward intervention compilation
donors.exploits: syntactically different causal subgraphs can implement identical boundary behavior and repeated recursive expansion then wastes symbolic search
preconditions: complete declared finite Boolean boundary behavior is executable
at least two structurally distinct training motifs share the exact semantic signature
held-out use passes exact semantic signature matching
effects: symbolic goal expansion falls on repeated equivalent causal motifs
assumptions: declared boundary variables capture all behavior relevant to replacement
finite Boolean equivalence is not generalized beyond its verified scope
